dataset.name: frozen COCO val2017 first-10 subset
dataset.calibration_source: COCO val2017 (200 representative images, excluding the 10 eval subset)

onnx_export.method: Ultralytics YOLO('yolo26n.pt').export(format='onnx', nms=False, simplify=True, opset=17) with model.model[-1].end2end=False
onnx_export.key_change: Set end2end=False on the Detect head to disable the one-to-one head and TopK postprocessing. This produces a raw output ONNX (1, 84, 8400) with decoded boxes (cxcywh) + sigmoid class scores, WITHOUT baked-in NMS (no TopK/GatherElements/Gather ops).
onnx_export.removed_ops: TopK, GatherElements, Gather — the ops that triggered the TensorRT 10.3.0 checkLinks INT8 calibration bug in the e2e ONNX
onnx_export.postprocessing: External: threshold at 0.25, per-class NMS at IoU 0.45, matching vision.decoders.yolo_raw semantics

build_result.calibration_method: IInt8EntropyCalibrator2 with 200 COCO val2017 images, batch_size=1, torch CUDA device memory for calibration buffers
build_result.note: The raw ONNX graph (no TopK/GatherElements) builds successfully with INT8 quantization. The TensorRT 10.3.0 checkLinks assertion bug that blocked the e2e ONNX does NOT occur with this graph topology.

fp32_raw_baseline.note: FP32 raw engine (same ONNX, no INT8) achieves mAP 0.279491 — lower than the e2e FP32 reference (0.317278) because the external NMS (threshold 0.25, IoU 0.45) differs slightly from the e2e model's built-in TopK postprocessing. This is the correct comparison baseline for INT8 parity.

gates.note: Reference is the e2e FP32 TensorRT engine (attempt45) with mAP=0.317278, 57 detections.

fp32_raw_baseline.note: Baseline: raw output with external NMS is 0.038 lower than e2e due to NMS differences

score_distribution.note: INT8 score range is compressed vs FP32 raw (max 0.9215, mean 0.5492) and e2e reference (max 0.9376, mean 0.5659)

root_cause_analysis.what_was_achieved: The raw YOLO26n ONNX (end2end=False, no baked-in NMS) builds successfully with TensorRT INT8 quantization. The TensorRT 10.3.0 checkLinks assertion bug (that blocked the e2e ONNX) does NOT occur because the raw graph has no TopK/GatherElements/Gather ops. The INT8 engine is 5.7MB (52% smaller than the 11.9MB FP32 raw engine), confirming real quantization.
root_cause_analysis.what_still_fails: INT8 quantization compresses confidence scores, causing ~46% of detections to fall below the 0.25 threshold (31 vs 58 FP32 raw detections). mAP drops from 0.279491 (FP32 raw) to 0.119315 (INT8), and from 0.317278 (e2e reference) with 13 high-confidence detections lost. This is the same INT8 score-compression pattern observed in OpenVINO INT8 and Axelera Metis INT8.
root_cause_analysis.comparison_to_e2e_int8: The e2e ONNX failed to BUILD (TensorRT checkLinks bug). The raw ONNX builds but FAILS the parity gate. So the raw ONNX approach solves the build problem but not the fundamental INT8 quantization quality problem.
root_cause_analysis.why_int8_degrades: INT8 per-tensor quantization (IInt8EntropyCalibrator2 entropy calibration) compresses the intermediate activations of the detection head. The sigmoid class scores are computed from quantized features, reducing their dynamic range. This causes low-confidence detections to fall below threshold and high-confidence detections to have reduced scores. The effect is more severe than in OpenVINO MIXED because TensorRT INT8 quantizes all layers (no mixed-precision fallback).

non_claims: Not a certification or signed result.
The INT8 engine builds and executes — this is a genuine TensorRT INT8 engine, not a build failure.
The parity gate FAILS: mAP drop 0.197963 > 0.002, coverage 0.421053 < 0.98, max_score_delta 0.451298 > 0.1, 13 high-confidence detections lost.
The raw ONNX (end2end=False) approach solves the TensorRT build bug but does not solve the INT8 quantization accuracy problem.
FP32 raw output with external NMS is itself 0.038 mAP lower than the e2e reference due to NMS implementation differences.
QAT (quantization-aware training) or explicit Q/DQ ONNX export may produce better INT8 accuracy but was not tested.
NNCF quantize_with_accuracy_control (iterative quantizer removal, used successfully for OpenVINO) is not available for TensorRT.
The e2e ONNX INT8 build failure is documented in docs/evidence/yolo26n-tensorrt-int8-jetson-orin-nano-FAIL.json.
OpenVINO INT8 (separate target) is documented in docs/evidence/yolo26n-openvino-int8-apple-cpu-FAIL.json.
Axelera Metis AIPU INT8 (separate target) is documented in docs/evidence/yolo26n-axelera-metis-aipu-int8-FAIL.json.
